items.stem: A model flags a transaction as likely fraud. What is the responsible next step?

options.text: Investigate before acting, treating the score as a signal not proof
options.rationale: Correct: a score is a signal that needs investigation, not proof.

options.text: Permanently block the customer with no review
options.rationale: Acting on a score alone can harm innocent customers.

options.text: Assume the model is always right

options.rationale: Alerts should be triaged, not ignored.

items.explanation: Correct: a score is a signal that needs investigation, not proof.

options.text: Keep human oversight of high-stakes actions like blocking

options.text: Monitor models for bias across customer groups
Automate permanent blocks with no review

options.text: Use customer data without regard to privacy rules

options.text: Too many false positives harm genuine customers and erode trust
options.rationale: Correct: false positives create friction and harm for innocent customers.

options.text: False positives have no customer impact

options.rationale: Both detection and false positives matter.

options.text: False positives always indicate real fraud
options.rationale: By definition they are wrongly flagged legitimate cases.
